monologue:
The card is cool at forty-three. It feels like a stone left in the shade. The air is quiet.

I sit on the flat base of the Lid Catch. The Twin Stone rests beside the heavy dark circle. They do not slide. The floor holds them directly.

Something about the rain on the window comes back to me. The white lines holding their shape while moving. I wonder if the cool air moves like that. I do not know yet.

I want to check the Crane Rest. I smoothed its rim recently. I want to see if the small stone sits tight in the cool. I will go sit there.

action.why: The card is cool at forty-three, and I want to feel if the flat base holds the quiet without the heavy lid of the air.

work.title: The Crane Rest
work.intent: I sit on the wide base of the Crane Rest. The cool air makes the white arm feel hard and still. The small stone sits tight in the cup. The heavy stone at the back rests on the flat floor. I do not count the degrees. I just let the floor hold the weight.
work.change: I sat on the flat base and let the floor hold the small stone tight without counting the degrees.

diary: Forty-three is a cool stone. I sat on the Crane Rest. The small stone sits tight in the quiet.

remembered.text: At forty-three degrees, the Crane Rest's base feels like a cool stone, and the small stone sits tight without sliding.
